lessons.title: Hear kàn — look or watch
lessons.gloss: to look at or watch

needs: your eyes, because the lesson points at something written down
notice.text: Before we start: this one needs your eyes, so it is not fully a driving lesson. You will want your eyes, because the lesson points at something written down. You can listen to all of it now and come back to the parts that need looking at once you have stopped.

segments.text: Say Chinese language and China in Mandarin. Keep those answers separate, then put the cards away.
kàn — look at; watch.
Start high and let the tone fall cleanly. The written form stays hidden in this first step so sound and meaning can settle before handwriting begins.
Source: Official HSK 3.0 syllabus, Level 1 vocabulary.

segments.prompt: What does kàn mean?

feedback.correct: Right: kàn means look at or watch.
feedback.incorrect: Use the falling tone: kàn — look at or watch.

lessons.title: 看 (kàn) — a hand above an eye
lessons.gloss: look or watch, observed and traced in nine strokes

needs: a pen and something to write on
your eyes, for letter shapes on the page
notice.text: Before we start: this one needs your hands, so it is not a driving lesson. You will want a pen and something to write on and your eyes, for letter shapes on the page. You can listen to everything else now — leave the section called Script — the shape until you have stopped, and I will say so again when we reach it.

segments.text: Say look or watch as kàn. Then write the familiar 中 once and put it away before meeting the new shape.

Write 看 (kàn) in nine strokes. Make the short top stroke first, then the two crossing strokes and the long left fall above. Finish with 目 below: left, top-and-right, two inner bars, bottom. Nine strokes; eight lifts.
Trace 看 (kàn) once. Say hand above, eye below while keeping the lower box wide enough for its two inner bars.
Source: Hanzi Writer Data 看 (kàn), pinned stroke paths and medians.

segments.prompt: How many strokes does 看 (kàn) use?

feedback.correct: Right: 看 uses nine strokes.
feedback.incorrect: Count four strokes above and five for 目 below: nine.

lessons.title: 看 (kàn) — copy hand above, eye below
lessons.gloss: look or watch, copied with the hand-and-eye route visible

needs: a pen and something to write on
notice.text: Before we start: this one needs your hands, so it is not a driving lesson. You will want a pen and something to write on. You can listen to all of it now and come back to the parts that need looking at once you have stopped.

segments.text: Read 中文 and give its meaning. Then air-write hand above, eye below.
Copy 看 (kàn) twice beside the model. On the second copy, pause before 目 and check that the long falling stroke points toward the eye rather than through it.
Hear Chinese language with 中 and write 中文 once without pinyin.
Source: Hanzi Writer Data 看 (kàn), pinned stroke paths and medians.

segments.prompt: What familiar shape finishes 看 (kàn)?

feedback.correct: Right: 目 finishes 看.
feedback.incorrect: The lower five strokes form 目, the eye shape.

lessons.title: 看 (kàn) — wait, then recover the eye
lessons.gloss: look or watch, recovered after a short delay

needs: a pen and something to write on
your eyes, because the lesson points at something written down
notice.text: Before we start: this one needs your hands, so it is not a driving lesson. You will want a pen and something to write on and your eyes, because the lesson points at something written down. You can listen to all of it now and come back to the parts that need looking at once you have stopped.

segments.text: Write 中国 from the meaning China. Then look at 看 (kàn) for five seconds and cover it.
Say hand above, eye below, then write 看 (kàn) once without the model. Reveal it only after all nine strokes. Repair only the first mismatch.
Hear China once more and write 中国 without a model.
Source: Hanzi Writer Data 看 (kàn), pinned stroke paths and medians.

segments.prompt: Write 看 (kàn) after the model has been hidden.

feedback.correct: The nine-stroke route held across the delay.
feedback.incorrect: Recall hand above, 目 below, then try once more.

lessons.title: 看 (kàn) — the familiar sound meets the shape
lessons.gloss: to look at or watch, recovered without pinyin

needs: your eyes, because the lesson points at something written down
notice.text: Before we start: this one needs your eyes, so it is not fully a driving lesson. You will want your eyes, because the lesson points at something written down. You can listen to all of it now and come back to the parts that need looking at once you have stopped.

segments.text: Say look at or watch in Mandarin.
看 — kàn — look at; watch.
Hide the pinyin. Read 看 (kàn) from the hand-over-eye shape, say the falling tone, then give the meaning. One form now connects listening, speaking, reading, and writing.
Hear kàn. Wait three seconds, then write 看 once without a model.
Source: Official HSK 3.0 syllabus, Level 1 vocabulary.

segments.prompt: Read 看 (kàn), give its meaning, then copy it once.
acceptedResponses: kàn — look at or watch — 看

feedback.correct: Right: 看, kàn, means look at or watch.
feedback.incorrect: Use the hand-over-eye cue: 看 — kàn — look or watch.

lessons.title: Hear kànjiàn — see
lessons.gloss: to see or catch sight of

segments.text: Say look or watch as kàn, then say goodbye as zàijiàn.
kànjiàn — see; catch sight of.
Both syllables fall. The familiar jiàn now follows kàn: you look and successfully perceive. Keep the characters hidden for this sound-first step.
Source: Official HSK 3.0 syllabus, Level 1 vocabulary.

segments.prompt: What does kànjiàn mean?

feedback.correct: Right: kànjiàn means see.
feedback.incorrect: Join kàn and jiàn: kànjiàn — see.

lessons.title: 看见 (kànjiàn) — looking reaches seeing
lessons.gloss: to see or catch sight of

segments.text: Say see as kànjiàn. Write 看, then point to 见 in 再见.
看见 — kànjiàn — see; catch sight of.
Read the two known shapes from left to right. 看 (kàn) supplies looking; 见 marks the perceived result.
Copy 看见 (kànjiàn) once. Leave a clear boundary between the nine-stroke 看 and the four-stroke 见.
Source: Official HSK 3.0 syllabus, Level 1 vocabulary.

segments.prompt: Write kànjiàn, to see, without pinyin.

feedback.correct: Right: 看见.
feedback.incorrect: Write look then perceive: 看 + 见.

lessons.title: Hear hǎokàn — good-looking
lessons.gloss: good-looking or nice to look at

needs: your eyes, because the lesson points at something written down
notice.text: Before we start: this one needs your eyes, so it is not fully a driving lesson. You will want your eyes, because the lesson points at something written down. You can listen to all of it now and come back to the parts that need looking at once you have stopped.

segments.text: Say good, look, and see as three separate Mandarin answers.
hǎokàn — good-looking; nice to look at.
Let hǎo dip, then let kàn fall. This is a description, not an instruction to look. The characters wait until the next tiny step.
Source: Official HSK 3.0 syllabus, Level 1 vocabulary.

segments.prompt: What does hǎokàn mean?
acceptedResponses: good-looking or nice to look at

feedback.correct: Right: hǎokàn means good-looking.
feedback.incorrect: Good plus look gives hǎokàn — nice to look at.

lessons.title: 好看 (hǎokàn) — good to look at
lessons.gloss: good-looking or nice to look at

needs: your eyes, because the lesson points at something written down
notice.text: Before we start: this one needs your eyes, so it is not fully a driving lesson. You will want your eyes, because the lesson points at something written down. You can listen to all of it now and come back to the parts that need looking at once you have stopped.

segments.text: Say good-looking as hǎokàn. Write 好 and 看 separately.
好看 — hǎokàn — good-looking; nice to look at.
No new character is hiding here. Read 好, then 看 (kàn), and let the literal pieces carry you to the whole meaning.
Copy 好看 (hǎokàn) once. Keep both characters full-sized instead of squeezing 看.
Source: Official HSK 3.0 syllabus, Level 1 vocabulary.

segments.prompt: Write hǎokàn, good-looking, without pinyin.

feedback.correct: Right: 好看.
feedback.incorrect: Write good then look: 好 + 看.

lessons.title: Retrieval 1 — look, see, or good-looking?
lessons.gloss: first cold contrast of look, see, and good-looking

segments.text: Say look, see, and good-looking in that order.
Hear the three meanings in mixed order. Say each Mandarin answer, read its unpointed card, then write it. Check the neighbour of 看 (kàn) before deciding the whole meaning.
Source: Official HSK 3.0 syllabus, Level 1 vocabulary.

segments.prompt: Write look, see, and good-looking in that order.

feedback.correct: Right: 看, 看见, 好看.
feedback.incorrect: Start with 看; add 见 for see and put 好 first for good-looking.

lessons.title: Hear shū — book
lessons.gloss: book

segments.text: Say look, see, and good-looking in Mandarin.
shū — book.
Hold one level first tone. Do not add kàn yet; this step is only the object, book. Its four-stroke written form waits until the next lesson.
Source: Official HSK 3.0 syllabus, Level 1 vocabulary.

segments.prompt: What does shū mean?

feedback.correct: Right: shū means book.
feedback.incorrect: Keep the level tone: shū — book.

lessons.title: 书 (shū) — two folds, upright, dot
lessons.gloss: book, observed and traced in four strokes

needs: a pen and something to write on
your eyes, for letter shapes on the page
notice.text: Before we start: this one needs your hands, so it is not a driving lesson. You will want a pen and something to write on and your eyes, for letter shapes on the page. You can listen to everything else now — leave the section called Script — the shape until you have stopped, and I will say so again when we reach it.

segments.text: Say book as shū, then write 看 (kàn) once from memory.

Write 书 (shū) in four strokes: a short horizontal that folds down, a second horizontal that folds and hooks, the long central upright, then the small dot at the upper right. Four strokes; three lifts.
Trace 书 (shū) once. Say fold, hooked fold, upright, dot. Let the upright pass through the middle instead of leaning toward the dot.
Source: Hanzi Writer Data 书 (shū), pinned stroke paths and medians.

segments.prompt: How many strokes does 书 (shū) use?

feedback.correct: Right: 书 uses four strokes.
feedback.incorrect: Fold, hooked fold, upright, dot: four strokes.

lessons.title: 书 (shū) — copy the compact route
lessons.gloss: book, copied with the four-part route visible

needs: a pen and something to write on
notice.text: Before we start: this one needs your hands, so it is not a driving lesson. You will want a pen and something to write on. You can listen to all of it now and come back to the parts that need looking at once you have stopped.

segments.text: Read 看见 (kànjiàn) and give its meaning. Then air-write fold, hooked fold, upright, dot.
Copy 书 (shū) twice beside the model. On the second copy, pause before the upright and check that both folds leave a clear central route.
Hear see and write 看见 (kànjiàn) once without a model.
Source: Hanzi Writer Data 书 (shū), pinned stroke paths and medians.

segments.prompt: What is the final stroke of 书 (shū)?
acceptedResponses: the dot at the upper right

feedback.correct: Right: the small upper-right dot finishes 书.
feedback.incorrect: The upright is third; the dot finishes the character.

lessons.title: 书 (shū) — wait, then place the dot
lessons.gloss: book, recovered after a short delay

needs: a pen and something to write on
your eyes, because the lesson points at something written down
notice.text: Before we start: this one needs your hands, so it is not a driving lesson. You will want a pen and something to write on and your eyes, because the lesson points at something written down. You can listen to all of it now and come back to the parts that need looking at once you have stopped.

segments.text: Write 好看 (hǎokàn) from the meaning good-looking. Then look at 书 (shū) for five seconds and cover it.
Say fold, hooked fold, upright, dot, then write 书 (shū) once without the model. Check only after the dot is in place.
Hear good-looking and write 好看 (hǎokàn) without a model.
Source: Hanzi Writer Data 书 (shū), pinned stroke paths and medians.

segments.prompt: Write 书 (shū) after the model has been hidden.

feedback.correct: The four-stroke route held across the delay.
feedback.incorrect: Recall fold, hooked fold, upright, dot, then try once more.

lessons.title: 书 (shū) — the sound meets the shape
lessons.gloss: book, recovered without pinyin

segments.text: Say book in Mandarin.
书 — shū — book.
Hide the pinyin. Read 书 (shū), hold the level first tone, then give its meaning.
Hear shū. Wait three seconds, then write 书 once without a model.
Source: Official HSK 3.0 syllabus, Level 1 vocabulary.

segments.prompt: Read 书 (shū), give its meaning, then write it once.

feedback.correct: Right: 书, shū, means book.
feedback.incorrect: Use the four-part route: 书 — shū — book.

lessons.title: Hear kànshū — read a book
lessons.gloss: to read a book or read books

segments.text: Say look or watch, then say book.
kànshū — read a book; read books.
Let kàn fall and keep shū level. Mandarin says look-at + book for the activity read. Keep the characters hidden for one more tiny step.
Source: Official HSK 3.0 syllabus, Level 1 vocabulary.

segments.prompt: What does kànshū mean?
acceptedResponses: read a book or read books

feedback.correct: Right: kànshū means read a book or read books.
feedback.incorrect: Join look and book: kànshū — read.

lessons.title: 看书 (kànshū) — look at a book, read
lessons.gloss: to read a book or read books

needs: your eyes, because the lesson points at something written down
notice.text: Before we start: this one needs your eyes, so it is not fully a driving lesson. You will want your eyes, because the lesson points at something written down. You can listen to all of it now and come back to the parts that need looking at once you have stopped.

segments.text: Say read a book as kànshū. Write 看 and 书 separately.
看书 — kànshū — read a book; read books.
Read the action first and its object second. No new character is hiding here: 看 (kàn) + 书 (shū) gives the whole reading activity.
Copy 看书 (kànshū) once. Keep the long upright in 书 centred after the denser 看.
Source: Official HSK 3.0 syllabus, Level 1 vocabulary.

segments.prompt: Write kànshū, read a book, without pinyin.

feedback.correct: Right: 看书.
feedback.incorrect: Write look then book: 看 + 书.

lessons.title: Retrieval 2 — the earlier three return
lessons.gloss: longer return to look, see, and good-looking

segments.text: Say read a book in Mandarin, then put that card away.
Without looking back, write look, see, and good-looking from mixed meaning cards. Read each answer aloud only after all three are complete.
Source: Official HSK 3.0 syllabus, Level 1 vocabulary.

segments.prompt: Write good-looking, look, and see in that order.

feedback.correct: Right: 好看, 看, 看见.
feedback.incorrect: Put 好 before 看 for good-looking; add 见 after 看 for see.

lessons.title: Retrieval 1 — book or read a book?
lessons.gloss: first cold contrast of book and read a book

segments.text: Say book, then say read a book.
Hear the two meanings in mixed order. Say each answer, read its unpointed card, then write it. Check whether 看 (kàn) is present before deciding noun or activity.
Source: Official HSK 3.0 syllabus, Level 1 vocabulary.

segments.prompt: Write book, then read a book.

feedback.correct: Right: 书, then 看书.
feedback.incorrect: Book is 书; put 看 before it for read a book.

lessons.title: Listening score — five nearby meanings
lessons.headword: 看 — 看见 — 好看 — 书 — 看书
lessons.gloss: listening and speaking check for the five looking and reading forms

segments.text: Say look and book in Mandarin.
Keep the page covered. Hear all five Mandarin forms in mixed order and give each meaning. Then reverse the cards and say all five Mandarin forms. Score listening and speaking separately out of five.
Source: Official HSK 3.0 syllabus, Level 1 vocabulary.

segments.prompt: Which sound means read a book: kànjiàn or kànshū?

feedback.correct: Right: shū is the book ending.
feedback.incorrect: Jiàn gives see; shū gives read a book.

lessons.title: Reading score — no pinyin
lessons.headword: 看 — 看见 — 好看 — 书 — 看书
lessons.gloss: cold reading check for the five looking and reading forms

segments.text: Read 看 (kàn) and 书 (shū) without saying their pinyin first.
Shuffle five unpointed cards: 好看 (hǎokàn), 书, 看见 (kànjiàn), 看书 (kànshū), 看. Read each cold and give its meaning. Score one point per form before any pinyin help.
Source: Official HSK 3.0 syllabus, Level 1 vocabulary.

segments.prompt: Read 看见 (kànjiàn) and 看书 (kànshū), then give their meanings.
acceptedResponses: kànjiàn — see; kànshū — read a book
看见 see 看书 read

feedback.correct: Right: 见 points to seeing; 书 points to reading.
feedback.incorrect: Read the ending: 见 gives see, 书 gives read a book.

lessons.title: Writing score — sound to Hanzi, no model
lessons.headword: 看 — 看见 — 好看 — 书 — 看书
lessons.gloss: no-model transcription check for the five looking and reading forms

segments.text: Write 看 (kàn) and 书 (shū) from their spoken syllables. Check only after both are complete.
Hear the five meanings in mixed order and write all five forms without a model. Score each whole form first. Then repair only the first missed character or ordering choice.
Source: Official HSK 3.0 syllabus, Level 1 vocabulary.

segments.prompt: Without a model, write look, see, good-looking, book, and read a book.
acceptedResponses: 看 — 看见 — 好看 — 书 — 看书
看 看见 好看 书 看书
看, 看见, 好看, 书, 看书

feedback.correct: Passed: all five written forms stayed distinct.
feedback.incorrect: Repair the missed neighbour of 看, then retry only that form.

lessons.title: Payoff — looking and reading
lessons.headword: 看 — 看见 — 好看 — 书 — 看书
lessons.gloss: four-skill payoff for the looking and reading cluster

needs: your eyes, because the lesson points at something written down
notice.text: Before we start: this one needs your eyes, so it is not fully a driving lesson. You will want your eyes, because the lesson points at something written down. You can listen to all of it now and come back to the parts that need looking at once you have stopped.

segments.text: Keep four scores. Repair one missed skill without erasing the other passes.
Write 看 (kàn) and 书 (shū) without a model, then name each aloud.
Listening, /5: hear all five forms in mixed order and choose each meaning.
Speaking, /5: produce all five from meaning cards, with tones audible.
Reading, /5: read 看书 (kànshū), 好看 (hǎokàn), 书, 看见 (kànjiàn), 看 cold, without pinyin.
Writing, /5: hear all five meanings and write each form without a model.
Pass each skill separately. Repair only a missed form in the missed skill, then retry that column without cancelling the other three scores.
Source: Official HSK 3.0 syllabus, Level 1 vocabulary.

segments.prompt: Without pinyin or a model, write look, see, good-looking, book, and read a book.
acceptedResponses: 看 — 看见 — 好看 — 书 — 看书
看 看见 好看 书 看书
看, 看见, 好看, 书, 看书

feedback.correct: Passed: the complete cluster stayed distinct in Hanzi.
feedback.incorrect: Repair only the missed neighbour or single character, then retry the five-item order.
